paragraphs: Creating is the act of producing a Game Object that previously did not exist in the game.
Effects that Create one or more Game Objects will direct where those Game Objects must go - the Game Objects are Created directly to the zones in question.
Prior to being Created, these Game Objects did not exist outside of the zone they were Created to. After being Created, they may change zones as appropriate for Game Objects of their type.
If a zone is not specified by the effect, the Game Object will be created to the appropriate zone for its type.
Permanents will be Created at any location on the Board that they can be played to.
Spells will be Created on the Chain.
Runes will be Created at base.
Legends will be Created in the Legend Zone.
Battlefields will be Created in the Battlefield Zone.
The zone a Game Object is created to can be specified implicitly by the Game Action being performed.
Example: “Play a 1 [M] Recruit token” specifies a zone where the token is Created to implicitly, by specifying the token is played and thus created on the chain.
Example: “Create a 1 [M] Recruit token” does not specify a zone, so the Recruit token will be created at any location on the board that it can be played to.
An effect that Creates a Game Object will specify the state and nature of the Game Object created.
If the Game Object is a token, it will follow the normal rules for tokens.
See rule 179. Tokens for more information.
If the effect specifies a Game Object is Created for a specific duration, it exists while that duration is ongoing, and ceases to exist once that duration ends.

If a Non-Token Game Object is Created from a finite set of choices made by a Linked Ability during deck building, only one of those Game Objects may exist in play at a time. If a player would Create a Game Object that already exists on the board or on the chain, that action is Negated.

Unless specified otherwise by the Game Effect that Creates a Game Object, any such Game Object is owned by the player who Created it. Control is established as usual for Game Objects of the appropriate type.
A Created permanent, rune, legend, or spell is controlled by its owner as it is Created.
A Created battlefield is uncontrolled as it is Created.
This action, when instructed, is usually formatted as "Create [X] at [Y]" or “Add [X] to [Y].”
Players may only Create Game Objects when directed to by Game Effects.
Burning is the act of moving cards from the top of a player’s Main Deck to their trash.
“When you burn” abilities or other Triggered Abilities that trigger on burning are executed after burning has occurred.
This action is formatted as "Burn X."
X is the number of cards to be Burned.
A player must Burn cards when instructed to do so by game effects or costs.

When Burning is part of an effect, then a player must Burn as many cards as possible. If instructed to burn more cards than they have in their main deck, they burn that many cards, burn out and then burn the rest.
See rule 432. Burn Out for more information.
Empowering is the act of rendering one or more Game Objects Empowered.
Empowered is a binary state. A Game Object is Empowered or it isn’t.
An Empowered Game Object can not be Empowered.
If a Game Object is instructed to be Empowered when it is already Empowered, nothing additional happens.
Some effects may grant a Game Object permission to be Empowered multiple times. Such an effect ignores this restriction. For these Game Objects, Empowered is not a binary state but a stacking status.
“Empowered” is a state for Game Objects on the board that other game effects and abilities can reference.
When a Game Object becomes Empowered as a result of the Empower game action, that is an event that can similarly be referenced by game effects and abilities.
Players may only Empower Game Objects when directed to by Game Effects.
Disempowering is the act of removing the Empowered status from one or more Game Objects.
Disempowering affects only cards that are currently Empowered.
Game effects that instruct a player to Disempower a card that is not currently Empowered will do nothing.
Disempowering a Game Object that has multiple Empowered statuses will remove one of those statuses.
Players may only Disempower Game Objects when directed to by Game Effects.
Skipping an event is the act of replacing that event with nothing.
Skip is an action that interacts with events and procedures of the turn.
Example: A card reads in part “Choose an enemy unit. Skip the next time that unit would move this turn.” This is a replacement effect that replaces the event of a unit moving with nothing.
Example: A card reads in part “Skip your Draw phase.” This is a replacement effect that replaces a player’s Draw Phase with nothing.
Example: A card reads in part “Choose a player. They skip their next point from conquering this turn.” This is a replacement effect that replaces the 1 point gained when conquering with nothing.
An event is the singular moment that results from a Game Action being performed or from a Game Object changing state.
See rule 367. Replacement Effects for more information.
Procedures of the turn include turns, phases, steps, and substeps.
Skip actions are usually formatted as “Skip [event or procedure of the turn].”
When an event or procedure of the turn is Skipped, it is replaced with nothing. Play proceeds accordingly.
Anything that triggers on the occurrence of the event or procedure of the turn does not trigger.
Players may only Skip events or procedures of the turn when directed to by Game Effects.
See rule 367. Replacement Effects for more information.
Paying a resource is the act of removing that resource from your Rune Pool.
Pay is an action that interacts with Energy and Power.
In order to qualify as a resource to be removed from the Rune Pool, the resource must be [1] or greater, or [C] or [A] or greater.
Example: [0] is not a resource that can be removed from the Rune Pool. As a cost, it is paid without performing the pay game action. This cannot be declined.
When a player is instructed to Pay a resource, that player may remove that resource from their Rune Pool if it exists there. If they choose not to, the instruction is negated.
If the instruction to Pay resources is part of paying costs for a card or ability, choosing not to pay those resources will cause the act of playing the card or ability to be undone.
See rule 358. Check Legality for more information.
If the instruction to Pay resources is part of paying any other cost, choosing not to pay those resources will prevent the execution of the associated effect.
See rule 201. Costs for more information.

Players may activate abilities that Add resources with the Reaction keyword at any time that they are instructed to Pay resources. Those abilities finalize and resolve immediately, ignoring normal restrictions.
See rule 430. Add for more information.
Players may only Pay resources when directed to by Game Effects.
Copying a Game Object is the act of adding or replacing some or all of the copyable traits of another Game Object with those of the Copied Game Object.
Copy Effects are rendered in the Copy Effects layer.
See rule 475. Layers for more information.

Some Game Objects may be created as a Copy of another Game Object. This is not a Copy Effect. The Copy in such a case is rendered with the same copyable traits as those of the Game Object it is a Copy of. It has no printed traits of its own that are subsequently replaced.

Example: Zilean, Time Mage is a unit that reads “Once each turn, if you would play a token unit while I'm at a battlefield, you may play that token and an additional copy of it instead.” The additional copy played by Zilean’s replacement effect has no printed traits of its own. Its printed traits are those of the token it is a copy of.
Players may only Copy Game Objects when directed to by Game Effects.

A Permanent changing its position from any space on the Board to another space on the Board is a Move, unless it is caused by a corrective Recall or an Attached Permanent changing locations to or with its Top-Most Card.
See rule 421. Move for more information.
A card changing game zones does not in itself constitute a Move.
There is no state for Permanents between locations.
Permanents are either at their Origin before Moving or their Destination after Moving.
Moving does not use the Chain, nor is it able to be Reacted to.
Moving is defined by the Origin and Destination of the Permanent that is changing locations.
The Origin is where the Permanent is starting from.
The Destination is where the Permanent is going to.

In Modes of Play with more than two players, Battlefields with Staged Combats or Combats in Progress are Invalid Destinations for Moves of all kinds (Standard Moves or otherwise) by Units controlled by Players not involved in those Combats or who don't already have units at that Battlefield.
In Modes of Play with teammates, Battlefields occupied by a player’s teammates are Invalid Destinations for Moves of all kinds (Standard Moves or otherwise) by Units that player controls.

If an action would require a Move that would cause a Unit to become present in a Location where it cannot move for any reason, such as a Battlefield with two players that are not the controller of the Unit performing this Move action are in a Combat or such a Combat is Staged, it instead Recalls.
See rule 456. Recalls for more information.
